'''''Centaurium scilloides''''', also known as '''perennial centaury''', is a flowering plant in the family [[Gentianaceae]]. It is native to [[Atlantic Europe]] ([[England]], western [[France]] and the northwestern [[Iberian Peninsula]]) and the [[Azores]]. Plants from the Azores have white flowers (as opposed to pink) and are genetically different with some treating it as a different species.<ref>{{cite web|title=Centaurium scilloides (L.f.) Samp.|url=https://acores.flora-on.pt/#/1Centaurium+scilloides|publisher=[[Flora-On]]|access-date=24 March 2021}}</ref><ref name=PSE>{{cite journal|last1=Prieto|first1=José Antonio Fernández|last2=Cires|first2=Eduardo|last3=Pérez|first3=René|last4=Bueno|first4=Álvaro|title=A new endemism for the Azores: the case of Centaurium scilloides (L. f.) Samp.|journal=[[Plant Systematics and Evolution]]|publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media]]|pages=1867–1879|doi=10.1007/s00606-012-0687-4|year=2012|volume=298|issue=10|s2cid=254048642|jstor=43558386|hdl=10651/23897|hdl-access=free}}</ref>

==History==
The species has been in cultivation in Britain since being introduced probably from the Azores by [[William Aiton]] in 1777.<ref name=bsbi>Rich, T.C.G.; Evans, S.B.; Evans, A.E.; Magnanon, S.; Hopkins, F.; Caldas, F.B.; Pryor, K.V.; Lledo, M.D. (2005)[https://archive.bsbi.org.uk/Wats25p275.pdf Distribution of the western European endemic Centaurium scilloides (L. f.) Samp. (Gentianaceae), Perennial Centaury] ''[[New Journal of Botany|Watsonia]]'' '''25''', pp. 275–281.</ref> In 1781, [[Carl Linnaeus the Younger]] described the species as ''Gentiana scilloides'', after F. Masson returned with a specieman from Azores.<ref name=PSE/>

Before its extinction in England in 1967, ''Centaurium scilloides'' was abundant in Cornwall, S.W. England where it was recorded from two settlements [[Porthgwarra]] and [[St Levan]] between 1952–1967. It survived in [[Pembrokeshire]], Wales where it grows in Newport since its discovery there in 1918.<ref name=bsbi/> In 2012, the species was recorded from the Azores, but was proven to be of different species.<ref name=PSE/>

==Description==
It is a perennial, herbaceous species, growing to a maximum height of {{convert|15|cm}}.<ref name=brc>{{cite web|url=https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/centaurium-scilloides|title=Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora - ''Centaurium scilloides''|access-date=8 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190708151629/https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/centaurium-scilloides|archive-date=8 July 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Habitat and distribution==
''Centaurium scilloides'' is found on coastal [[cliff]]s and [[dune]]s grassland.<ref name=brc/> It grows all along the [[Atlantic Ocean|Atlantic]] coast of [[Europe]].

==Conservation==
As of 2001, its conservation status was evaluated as 'Endangered' by the [[International Union for Conservation of Nature|IUCN]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhm.ac.uk/our-science/data/uk-species/species/centaurium_scilloides.html|title=Natural History Museum London - ''Centaurium scilloides''|access-date=8 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190708151627/https://www.nhm.ac.uk/our-science/data/uk-species/species/centaurium_scilloides.html|archive-date=8 July 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Uses==
In Japan, ''C. scilloides'', is popularly used for decoration purposes. It is used as a border in rock gardens and grows in pots and on verandas.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Nishikawa|first1=Kazutaka|last2=Shimomura|first2=Koichiro|last3=Kayano|first3=Toshiaki|last4=Ishimaru|first4=Kanji|title=Shoot Regeneration in Root Cultures of Centaurium scilloides|journal=Plant Biotechnology|volume=14|issue=2|year=1997|doi=10.5511/plantbiotechnology.14.117}}</ref>
